The firm’s fee‑based model gives it some pricing power, but higher borrowing costs and modest capex needs temper the upside.

Higher interest rates raise the cost of capital for the company, eroding net interest margins.
The upward‑sloping yield curve raises borrowing costs for the operating partnership, squeezing cash flow.
Growth in servicer portfolio may drive capex, but higher rates increase financing costs, moderating investment.
Stable economic conditions support liquidity and reduce working capital strain, improving cash conversion.
